comparison: Both evaluate HepG4-seq method validation (C19-C25, C32). OpenEval finds the method well-supported with comprehensive experimental validation. Peer reviewers accept it as 'a useful antibody-free method' but one reviewer notes the comparison to existing datasets 'does not unequivocally demonstrate superiority.' Agreement on basic functionality, disagreement on superiority claims.

Both address HepG4-seq sensitivity and capability (C122-C123). OpenEval emphasizes validation through helicase inhibition experiments. Peer reviewers acknowledge the method as 'useful' and 'novel' for mapping native G4s, accepting basic capability though questioning superiority claims.

Both evaluate HBD-seq method validation (C33-C34). OpenEval finds the method well-supported with robust peak detection and appropriate controls. Peer reviewers express significant concerns about specificity, stating 'sensitivity to RNase does not demonstrate HBD-seq specifically reports RNA:DNA hybrids' and questioning whether it 'performed satisfactorily.' Major disagreement on method validity.

Both evaluate cell type-specific co-localization patterns (C35-C38, C44-C48, C115, C124-C125). OpenEval finds substantial quantitative differences well-documented. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'extensive data on distribution' and 'cell-type-specific distributions' as accepted descriptive findings. Strong agreement on these observational results.

Both address transcriptional associations of co-localized peaks (C39-C40, C51-C52, C116). OpenEval emphasizes RNA-seq evidence for regulatory roles. Peer reviewers accept these as part of the descriptive characterization showing structures 'localize at active promoters and enhancers of transcriptionally active genes.' Agreement on descriptive findings.

Both evaluate helicase inhibition effects on transcription (C41-C43, C117-C118). OpenEval finds functional evidence linking G4 accumulation to transcriptional changes well-supported. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the descriptive characterization without raising specific concerns. Agreement on these experimental results.

Both address transcriptional regulatory context (C134-C135). OpenEval emphasizes statistical support for higher expression at co-localized peaks. Peer reviewers acknowledge structures 'predominantly localize at active promoters and enhancers' but note work 'remains primarily descriptive.' Agreement on observations, difference in emphasis on mechanistic depth.

Both evaluate chromatin context of co-localized peaks (C54-C65). OpenEval finds clear associations with active chromatin states well-supported, though notes limited direct evidence for RNA involvement. Peer reviewers accept these chromatin overlap findings as part of the descriptive characterization without specific challenges. Agreement on chromatin associations.

Both evaluate Dhx9 regulatory role through knockout experiments (C69-C74, C119-C120). OpenEval finds functional evidence clear with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers acknowledge the study 'consolidates the role of Dhx9' but state evidence is 'still incomplete' and provides 'limited mechanistic insight.' Agreement on basic findings, disagreement on sufficiency of mechanistic evidence.

Both evaluate Dhx9 binding and direct regulation (C78-C90). OpenEval finds CUT&Tag data demonstrate genome-wide binding with appropriate validation. Peer reviewers acknowledge findings but express that mechanistic insight remains limited and evidence is incomplete. Agreement on observational data, disagreement on mechanistic depth.

Both address regulatory complexity and redundancy (C128-C132). OpenEval notes only ~8.5% of Dhx9-bound peaks show changes, suggesting redundancy with other helicases. Peer reviewers accept these findings on complexity as part of the descriptive characterization. Agreement on the complexity of regulation.

Both evaluate functional consequences of Dhx9 loss on mESC phenotypes (C91-C100, C121). OpenEval finds multiple lines of functional evidence consistently demonstrate altered pluripotency and differentiation. Peer reviewers acknowledge the study 'reveals that Dhx9 can affect self-renewal and differentiation capacities' and accept phenotypic observations. Strong agreement on phenotypic results.

Both evaluate dynamic G4 regulation through helicase inhibition (C26-C31, C117-C118). OpenEval finds strong evidence for G4 accumulation with substantial ~10-fold increase. Peer reviewers accept these data as part of the descriptive characterization of G4 dynamics without specific concerns. Agreement on experimental findings.

Both address transcriptional consequences of helicase inhibition (C117-C118). OpenEval emphasizes consistency with known G4 functions. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the descriptive work. Agreement on these observations.

Both evaluate methodological comparison between HepG4-seq and existing methods (C101-C106). OpenEval finds substantial concordance with better resolution, though notes some interpretations remain speculative. Peer reviewers acknowledge comparison as 'important addition' but state it 'does not unequivocally demonstrate superiority.' Agreement on comparison data, disagreement on interpretation of superiority.

Both evaluate HBD-seq validation through comparison with existing methods (C107-C114). OpenEval finds reasonable concordance with improved signal quality, acknowledging unresolved specificity questions. Peer reviewers note comparison data but express persistent concerns about HBD-seq specificity and whether it 'performed satisfactorily.' Agreement that comparison data exist, disagreement on whether they resolve specificity concerns.

OpenEval evaluates CTCF binding connection (C126-C127) as uncertain, noting purely correlative evidence without functional validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these CTCF-related claims.

Both address regulatory complexity and redundancy (C133). OpenEval notes this as a discussion point supported by limited Dhx9-dependent changes and altered helicase expression. Peer reviewers accept findings on complexity and 'interplay between G4s and R-loops' as part of descriptive characterization. Agreement on regulatory complexity.
